scope: Theorem 3.11 (Eventual reversal at categoricity cardinals) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each infinite cardinal θ there is a cardinal bK(θ) such that, whenever κ ≥ bK(θ) is a categoricity cardinal, M ∈ K has size κ, f : M −→ M is strong, and ā is a tuple of length at most θ in M, there is a strong g : M −→ M with g(f(ai)) = ai for every coordinate i. The bound concerns all sufficiently large categoricity cardinals, of arbitrary cofinality. No equality of the form κθ = κ is assumed.
